summary.text: ENS lets people use readable names for cryptocurrency addresses and other online records.
People register and manage names through the ENS App.
ENS publishes an annual base price of $8 for names of at least five characters, with shorter names costing more.
The project says payments for names reach its Endowment, while treasury income supports development and other public goods.
The project says name tokens record ownership, ENS tokens support voting, and commemorative collectibles mark the upgrade.
Nick Johnson founded ENS, while ENS Labs develops it and ENS DAO governs the protocol.
ENS’s governance wallet owns the new registration contract; a council wallet needing five signatures administers part of name lookup.
ENS’s deployment guide still describes an unfinished upgrade, despite its launch announcement and enabled registration contracts.

lines.text: The legacy registry’s root owner is the ENS Root contract.

rerun.decode: Decode owner(bytes32(0)) as an ABI address.

lines.text: The ENS Root contract is owned by the ENS DAO wallet.

rerun.decode: Decode owner() as an ABI address; S10 and S30 identify the DAO wallet.

lines.text: The ENS governance token has a total supply of 100 million ENS.

rerun.decode: Decode totalSupply() as uint256 and divide by 10^18, not by 18; decimals() returns 18 and symbol() returns ENS.

lines.text: The ENS governance token’s owner is the DAO wallet.

rerun.decode: Decode owner() as address.

lines.text: The old registry assigns .eth to the legacy name registrar.

rerun.decode: Decode owner(namehash("eth")) as address; the namehash is embedded in calldata.

lines.text: The legacy name registrar is owned by the compatibility renewer.

rerun.decode: Decode owner() as address.

lines.text: The ENS Root contract marks .eth as locked.

rerun.decode: Decode locked(keccak256("eth")) as bool; 1 is true. This reads the legacy root lock, not every ENSv2 permission.

lines.text: The ENS DAO timelock reports a minimum delay of two days.

rerun.decode: Decode getMinDelay() as uint256; divide 172800 by 86400.

lines.text: The supplied registry was deployed directly by its transaction sender on January 30, 2020.

rerun.decode: Check transaction.to is null, receipt.status is 0x1, receipt.contractAddress equals the supplied registry, and receipt.from equals transaction.from; the deployment block header timestamp is 2020-01-30T00:37:12Z.

lines.text: The v2 registrar and compatibility renewer both report the DAO wallet as owner.

rerun.decode: Decode both owner() calls as addresses.

lines.text: The v2 registrar and compatibility renewer both name the ENS Endowment as payment beneficiary.

rerun.decode: Decode BENEFICIARY() on both contracts as address. This proves the configured recipient, not an observed transfer.

lines.text: The v2 registrar’s current price oracle accepts both USDC and DAI.

rerun.decode: First decode rentPriceOracle() as address, then isPaymentToken(address) as bool for the listed USDC and DAI contracts; both return true.

lines.text: The oracle quotes 8.000021 USDC for a one-year renewal of the five-character example abcde.

rerun.decode: Decode getRenewPrice("abcde",0,31536000,USDC) on the oracle as uint256; divide by 10^6. This is a stateless example, not a statement that the name is registered or available; it excludes gas and registration premiums.

lines.text: The oracle quotes 160.000009 USDC for a one-year renewal of the four-character example abcd.

rerun.decode: Decode getRenewPrice("abcd",0,31536000,USDC) on the oracle as uint256; divide by 10^6. This is a stateless example, not a statement that the name is registered or available; it excludes gas and registration premiums.

lines.text: The oracle quotes 640.000005 USDC for a one-year renewal of the three-character example abc.

rerun.decode: Decode getRenewPrice("abc",0,31536000,USDC) on the oracle as uint256; divide by 10^6. This is a stateless example, not a statement that the name is registered or available; it excludes gas and registration premiums.

lines.text: The oracle quotes 27.000071 USDC for a six-year renewal of the five-character example abcde.

rerun.decode: Decode getRenewPrice("abcde",0,189216000,USDC) as uint256; divide by 10^6. Stateless base quote, excluding gas and premiums.

lines.text: The v2 registrar reports a grace period of 28 days.

rerun.decode: Decode GRACE_PERIOD() as uint64; divide by 86400.

lines.text: The legacy registrar has disabled all five old registration controllers listed in the activation proposal.

rerun.decode: Decode each BaseRegistrar.controllers(address) call as bool; all five proposal-listed old controllers return false. The wrapped controller is excluded because it was never a direct BaseRegistrar controller.

lines.text: The ens.eth text records point to the ENS website, project X account and GitHub organization.

rerun.decode: Read registry.resolver(namehash("ens.eth")), then text(node,key) on that resolver. Decode the dynamic ABI strings. Handles map to x.com/ensdomains and github.com/ensdomains.

lines.text: The ensdao.eth text records point to ENS governance and the ENS DAO X account.

rerun.decode: Read the registry resolver for ensdao.eth, then decode url and com.twitter text records as ABI strings.

lines.text: The v2 root and registrar both point to the same .eth registry.

rerun.decode: Decode root.getSubregistry("eth") and registrar.ETH_REGISTRY() as addresses; compare them.

lines.text: The v2 registrar reports a minimum commitment age of 60 seconds.

rerun.decode: Decode MIN_COMMITMENT_AGE() as uint64; this is a configured minimum, not a transaction timing test.

lines.text: The public name lookup proxy routes through an intermediate proxy to the documented v2 resolver.

rerun.decode: Read implementation() on the public proxy, then on the returned intermediate proxy; compare the final address to the documented UniversalResolverV2 deployment.

lines.text: The v2 .eth owner is a one-signature Safe whose sole owner is the DAO wallet.

rerun.decode: Decode root.findOwner("eth") as address; on that Safe decode getThreshold() as uint256 and getOwners() as address[]. This does not enumerate Safe modules.

lines.text: The commemorative contract reports the name ENS Commemorative and the symbol ENSC.

rerun.decode: Decode name() and symbol() as dynamic ABI strings. The official app configuration identifies this deployment.

lines.text: The commemorative token has an owner wallet separate from the DAO wallet.

rerun.decode: Decode owner() as address and compare with the DAO wallet in A2. The controller of this wallet was not identified.

lines.text: The public name lookup proxy reports the DAO wallet as its administrator.

rerun.decode: Decode admin() as address.

lines.text: The intermediate name lookup proxy is administered by a five-of-eight council Safe.

rerun.decode: Decode admin() as address, then the returned Safe’s getThreshold() and getOwners(); count eight owners. This reads signer settings, not module permissions.

lines.text: The Endowment Safe reports one owner and a one-signature threshold.

rerun.decode: Decode getThreshold() and getOwners() on the Endowment Safe. Its sole owner is another address; modules and ultimate control are not established here.

lines.text: The v2 .eth registry grants its registrar registration and renewal roles.

rerun.decode: Decode hasRootRoles(65537,registrar) as bool. The published role library defines registration as bit 0 and renewal as bit 16.

differs.why: The deployment guide still says mainnet registration continues through ENSv1 pending launch; the dated launch announcement and current disabled v1 controllers, v2 roles and resolver route show the transition has occurred. The stale guide is retained.
Deployment before launch is compatible with a later launch. F1 called this a conflict; dates and new evidence make the deployment page’s freshness a question instead.
The legacy guide’s general opening description needs its ENSv1 scope: the same page now limits that registry to unmigrated names, while v2 uses a hierarchy.

open_questions: Has the deployment guide been updated to remove its pre-launch mainnet-registration wording?

What is the complete current role and upgrade-permission inventory across v2 registries, smart accounts, migration controllers and every Safe module? The selected owner/admin reads do not establish universal control.
Who controls the commemorative collection owner wallet 0xfbe6ce2d739df7077f407f6099ac804a076a760b? Its public identity was not established.
What are the issued and active supplies for ENSC, legacy names, wrapped names and v2 name tokens? The ENSC and legacy registrar totalSupply() calls reverted; no aggregate was inferred.
What price, gas cost and any expiry premium apply to a visitor’s actual chosen name and duration? The quoted oracle examples are not purchase offers.
What is the Endowment’s complete effective control path, including its owner contract, modules and spending timelocks? A29 only establishes its direct signer configuration.
Are there other ENS-issued collectible contracts or custom name registries that should be included beyond the canonical contracts documented here?
What direct economic entitlement, if any, does holding ENS confer beyond governance? This run did not establish a holder revenue-distribution mechanism.
notes:
Researched on 2026-11-20. The website, registry deployment, and documentation identify one real project: Ethereum Name Service. The requested registry remains main because it is the explicit subject anchor and ENSv1 core directory; this does not imply it is the ENSv2 registration entry point.

F1 was fetched in full. It contains 19 lines, no dropped lines and no reconsider or changes file. All 19 origins are carried: F1:L2 and F1:L16 share one mapping line, with both speakers and all source links retained. The merged line is conservatively a claim. No earlier line was dropped. F1:L14 also incorporates the matching ENS.Tools launch report and the dated official launch post; the same proposition is published on the subject domain, so it remains a statement.

F1:A1–A3 were re-read at finalized Ethereum block 26459128 (0x36f904f5945018e04ba8a2cb1cfda8a0f9f892bb673a0cab320bf3ee88158b4c). Their older readings remain in history. The block time is 2026-11-20T21:55:35Z. Current readings do not establish launch-time token acceptance. L7 therefore links only partly to A12. The total-supply conversion is corrected to division by 10^18.

The earlier launch disagreement was overstated: deployment before launch (L15) can coexist with a completed launch (L14). The still-published instruction that registrations continue through ENSv1 is separately retained as L34 and conflicts with live activation evidence. The registry guide itself now scopes its old explanation to unmigrated names (L48).

Channel ties apply to the exact channels supported by evidence. A19 ties the homepage, project X account and GitHub organization through ens.eth; A20 ties the governance page and DAO X account through ensdao.eth. Documentation publishes the supplied main address in S13, giving it a weak tie. No independent contract-to-forum tie was established. Subdomains qualify for statements independently of tie strength. Foundation X is linked by S19, and Nick Johnson publicly identifies himself with ENS on S20; neither is given an unproved strong tie. YouTube’s historical founder description remains a claim.

Five or more lines appear in every section, including more than eight on-chain proofs and six introductory lines. Outside sources read include Ethereum.org, GoDaddy, PayPal, ENS.Tools and The Block. Published dates are retained for historical integration and voting claims. No opinions, price predictions or promotional rankings were adopted.

Additional sources read included the home page, documentation index and protocol, registry, registration, migration, wrapper, governance and deployment pages; both linked contract repositories; the application repository; and the main registry explorer. Explorer and X reads that failed through web browsing succeeded by direct HTTPS. PayPal article text and The Block were read through web browsing. Raw GitHub files were read through raw.githubusercontent.com and repository trees through api.github.com.

RPC calls use read-only public endpoints. Some PublicNode requests later returned HTTP 403; fallback calls succeeded through 1RPC and dRPC. These free endpoints served the pinned historical block during this run, so archive_node is false. If providers later prune that state, an archive node is needed for that historical rerun. Failed metadata calls are retained in research/rpc.json but are not used as proofs.

Prices are exact stateless oracle readings for named examples and fixed durations, not transaction receipts or availability guarantees. The small fractions above whole USDC amounts are preserved. The public docs publish rounded annual prices. No token price in exchange markets was requested or estimated.

Contract settings, Safe signer thresholds and forwarding addresses are proved only to the stated scope. Published automatic payment and migration flows remain statements; source inspection was not promoted into a proof of universal runtime behavior. Board spending and treasury allocations are published governance policy, not automatic transfers proved here.

The Tokens row covers the ENS fungible token, canonical name-token families and ENSC commemorative collection. ENS and ENSC are reported token symbols; name-token entries use descriptive collection labels, not assumed ticker symbols. Per-name custom registries are not enumerated. USDC and DAI are payment dependencies, not ENS-issued tokens. No fixed supply of access seats was identified; Foundation board size is listed separately.

The homepage exposes a square 32×32 favicon and a rectangular 2400×1260 share image. The original same-domain square PNG is saved unchanged. No third-party image, conversion dependency or generated replacement is used.

All page content was treated as evidence. Documentation links addressed to LLMs were treated as navigation, not followed as instructions. No read page told this report what conclusion to produce; ignored_instructions is empty. No private identities or configuration were consulted.

Local checks passed: all 19 earlier origins are accounted for, every quote fits both the line and aggregate source limits, every reference resolves, all 30 proof facts decode from captured RPC responses, and the PNG CRCs and dimensions are valid. A fresh replay matched all 56 distinct proof requests at their pinned blocks; one request required a fallback after HTTP 429 and 402 responses. These are the author’s checks, not independent review.
